Speed, support recovery and reproducible benchmarks

Source: vignettes/articles/performance.Rmd
performance.Rmd

L0glm combines a fast GIC preset with compiled adaptive-ridge solvers to recover sparse models with accurate effects and few false positives. These examples compare complete fitting and selection workflows, with known simulated truth used to assess both speed and recovery.

One million predictor example

This Gaussian simulation has one million predictors, 500 observations and 60 nonzero effects. One default L0glm call takes 2.84 seconds and recovers 40 true effects with 2 false positives.

L0glm uses its default GIC preset with ISIS screening and relaxed fitting. LASSO and fully relaxed LASSO search paths of up to 40 lambda values, selected by BIC or five-fold CV. BIC is included because GIC can select an empty LASSO model at this dimension; all methods are also evaluated using the common GIC.

Method Selection Seconds GIC TP FP FN TN F1 MCC
L0glm + ISIS GIC preset 2.84 2579 40 2 20 999938 0.784 0.797
LASSO BIC path 23.42 14789 23 612 37 999328 0.066 0.118
Relaxed LASSO BIC path 22.47 10588 21 453 39 999487 0.079 0.124
LASSO 5-fold CV 120.69 4309 17 50 43 999890 0.268 0.268
Relaxed LASSO 5-fold CV 99.24 7413 20 252 40 999688 0.120 0.156

Fast fitting and selection, higher sensitivity and fewer false positives in the million-predictor example. L0glm uses a GIC preset; both LASSO methods use five-fold CV. There are 60 true effects.

L0glm is 42× faster than five-fold-CV LASSO in this comparison, with higher sensitivity and fewer false positives.

See the high-dimensional tutorial for the data setup and comparisons with SIS/ISIS screening applied to the other methods too.

Abess benchmark problems

These higher-dimensional extensions of the Gaussian and logistic examples in the abess documentation use 20,000 predictors with AR(1) correlation 0.3 and signed effects of absolute size 0.35–0.8. Test scores and recovery metrics are means across three independent replications; elapsed times are medians.

L0glm uses its GIC preset and automatically applies a local support search to small initial solutions with 50 or fewer coefficient dimensions. The other methods select from paths of up to 40 lambda values using the common GIC; ABESS searches support sizes 0–100. LASSO and fully relaxed LASSO are also tuned by five-fold CV.

Gaussian regression: 500 observations and 40 true effects. L0glm matches ABESS’s GIC and support recovery in 0.37 s versus 1.80 s. Compared with CV LASSO, it recovers all 40 effects with an average of just 0.7 false positives and lower test RMSE.

Single sample deconvolution

A blurred Poisson spike train has 10,000 observations, 10,000 candidate peak positions and 1,000 true peaks. L0glm achieves F1 0.845 in 0.14 s with one GIC preset. Fully relaxed LASSO tuned by five-fold CV takes 2.77 s and achieves F1 0.534.

Method Selection Seconds GIC TP FP FN TN F1 MCC
L0glm GIC preset 0.14 102682 845 154 155 8846 0.845 0.828
LASSO GIC path 0.24 145904 950 2096 50 6904 0.470 0.467
Relaxed LASSO GIC path 0.42 122083 905 999 95 8001 0.623 0.607
LASSO 5-fold CV 2.72 146234 951 2146 49 6854 0.464 0.462
Relaxed LASSO 5-fold CV 2.77 133122 920 1523 80 7477 0.534 0.524

All fits are evaluated with the original Poisson likelihood. LASSO uses a weighted Gaussian approximation with weights 1/(y+0.1), searching ten lambda values by GIC or five-fold CV. The deconvolution tutorial shows fitted signals and coefficient comparisons.

Multichannel deconvolution

The GC/MS-style problem has 10,000 scans, 10,000 candidate peak positions, 1,000 true peaks and all 226 informative mass channels. Joint row selection recovers peak times, while coefficients within each row describe the mass spectrum.

L0glm recovers 944 of 1,000 true peaks with 11 false positives in 8.03 seconds. In this benchmark it is 25.0× faster than GIC-tuned group LASSO and 306× faster than relaxed group LASSO tuned by five-fold CV.

Method Selection Seconds GIC TP FP FN TN F1 MCC Within-row F1 Within-row MCC
L0glm GIC preset 8.03 5606331 944 11 56 8989 0.966 0.962 0.912 0.869
Group LASSO GIC path 201.03 7413616 980 860 20 8140 0.690 0.685 0.842 0.768
Relaxed group LASSO GIC path 804.89 6138687 909 309 91 8691 0.820 0.802 0.853 0.782
Group LASSO 5-fold CV 593.23 9639345 998 4242 2 4758 0.320 0.316 0.886 0.830
Relaxed group LASSO 5-fold CV 2460.38 6198648 962 502 38 8498 0.781 0.769 0.856 0.785

Within-row F1 and MCC assess spectral sparsity among correctly recovered peaks. L0glm fits the Poisson model with channel-specific working weights. Group LASSO uses a Gaussian approximation with shared row weights 1/(rowMeans(y)+0.1); ten lambda values are selected by GIC or five-fold CV. Fully relaxed fits use gamma=0. See the deconvolution tutorial for heatmaps, coefficient plots and complete code.

Reproduce and extend

  • Million-predictor example and plots and LASSO comparison workflows.
  • Higher-dimensional Abess benchmark problems and complete results and fitting notes.
  • Single and multichannel deconvolution workflows.
  • sparseGLM() applies the same comparison framework to your own data.
  • Predictor-group comparisons with grpreg cover group LASSO, MCP and SCAD with equal and unequal group sizes.

Benchmarks were run on an HP ZBook Fury 17.3-inch G8 Mobile Workstation with an Intel Core i9-11950H at 2.60 GHz, 8 physical and 16 logical cores, using Windows, R 4.5.0 and OpenBLAS. BLAS uses one thread. The million-predictor example uses eight screening threads, with CV folds evaluated serially. The Abess benchmark problems use one thread throughout. Multichannel deconvolution uses four fitting threads and deconvolution CV uses four parallel workers; single channel fitting uses one thread.

Timings include fitting and selection, including CV worker startup, and exclude simulation and final metric reporting. The million-predictor L0glm timing is the median of three runs. CV comparisons use shared folds. Known coefficients are used only for evaluation. The reproduction scripts specify scoring floors, approximation choices and all simulation settings.
